question: The politics screen whole: CPoliticsView's elements, the parties, the cabinet and the minister choice, the laws and the law choice, the C*Change history classes, and the top bar's politics button.

structs.name: CPoliticsView
structs.comment: The politics screen: country view index 3 (the fourth view the in-game screen makes, its CCountryView view_index 3), main window `country_politics`, second window `topcolor_politics`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md, section D.

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::CPoliticsView
addresses.comment: **The politics screen's constructor.** CCountryView::CCountryView(this, idler, 'country_politics', 'topcolor_politics', 3) - view index 3 - then vftable 0x15D1854 and ten button glues: +0xB8 OnMinisterSelectCancel, +0xE4 OnLawWindowCancel, +0x110 OnPolicyWindowCancel, +0x13C OnMobilize, +0x168 OnDemobilize, +0x194 OnRevolt, +0x1C0 OnSelectWindowBack, +0x1EC OpenPuppetSelection, +0x220 OpenLiberateSelection; the two pending tags +0x218 and +0x24C set to '---'/0. Then BuildWidgets, BindPopularityChart, UpdateOrganisationBars, FillPartyLegend, and the law window's `cancel` hooked to +0xE4. One caller, the in-game screen's view list at 0x659B79 (`new 0x258`). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md, D.1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing 0x6BADA0-0x6BB1C9: `mov esi,[ebp+8]` is this, [ebp+0xC] the idler handed to 0x6EB040 with the two window names and `push 3`; each glue is {vftable 0x15D1BC0, this, handler, 0...} at a 0x2C stride; `ret 8`; eax = esi on exit. Wrong if any glue handler address differs from the table above (each is a literal store).

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 1: resets the vftable and the nine glues' vftables to CButtonObserver, calls the base destructor 0x6EB2D0, frees when bit 0 of flags is set. Ghidra's RTTI pass calls this 'CPoliticsView constructor', which it is not.
addresses.evidence: 0x6BB1D0-0x6BB22F, `ret 4`, the `test byte [ebp+8],1` / free pair; CPoliticsView's vftable slot 1 holds it (vtable.py).

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::Rebuild
addresses.comment: Slot 0: CCountryView::Rebuild (the windows made again), then BuildWidgets, BindPopularityChart, UpdateOrganisationBars, FillPartyLegend, UpdateOrganisationBars **again**, and the law window's `cancel` hooked to +0xE4. Returns the base Rebuild's answer. Who calls slot 0 was not read.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6BB240-0x6BB347: the five calls at 0x6BB260-0x6BB281 in that order (0x6BE220 twice), then 'law_selection_window' / 'cancel' and the glue's slot 1 with esi+0xE4; bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::Show
addresses.comment: Slot 2: shows `topcolor_politics` then `country_politics`, the automation line (slot 11), RefreshCabinetRows, FillPopularityChart, UpdateOrganisationBars; hides minister_select_win, law_selection_window, policy_selection_window, puppet_select and liberate_select; FillGovernmentLabels, FillLawList, FillOccupationList; `faction_symbol_icon` given frame CFaction +0x3C where the played country's faction (CCountry +0xD8) is real (its slot 7), else hidden; last, the main window's slot 30 with 'politics_view' (the group string the in-game screen dispatches tooltips by). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md, D.1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6BC0E0-0x6BC486, the calls and the five window names in that order; the frame is `mov ecx,[ecx+0xD8]; mov ecx,[ecx+0x3C]` pushed to the icon's slot 18 (0x6BC3B1-0x6BC3C2). Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 6, per frame while the view is open (its slot 7). (1) RefreshCabinetRows when minister_list1 is visible. (2) Where any laws_listbox row's law (+0x7C) is not the played country's law of that group (+0x628[group->index]), FillLawList. (3) policies_listbox's slot 31. (4) The three buttons on the same spot: a government in exile (CCountry +0x95) shows `revolt` alone, enabled where 0x50AE40(country) answers yes; otherwise `revolt` is hidden and `demobilize` is shown when mobilised (+0x94), `mobilize` when not, and both are disabled at war (+0xACC) and enabled at peace. (5) convoys_val / allies_val / bombs_val in `strat_warfare` = FormatStratWarfareImpact of CCountry +0x118C / +0x1190 / +0x1194. (6) create_puppet: with a pending released country at +0x218 it is disabled, and the pending tag is cleared once that country owns a province; otherwise enabled where GetPossibleVassals is non-empty. liberate_country the same with +0x24C and GetPossibleLiberations (0x4EDED0). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md, D.1.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6BB350-0x6BC01D read end to end: the IsOpen test at 0x6BB37B; byte +0x47 of the list box at 0x6BB3C1; the law loop 0x6BB4B0-0x6BB4D2; the +0x95/+0x94/+0xACC tests at 0x6BB559, 0x6BB72F, 0x6BB8E2 with button slots 13/14 (show/hide) and 46/47 (+0xB8 enable, +0xBC disable); the three strat-warfare finds at 0x6BBA59, 0x6BBB79, 0x6BBC99; +0x21C/+0x250 at 0x6BBDA5/0x6BBEDE. Two bare `ret`s, both exits of one frame.

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall CPoliticsView::BuildTooltip(CPoliticsView* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element) @EAX
addresses.comment: Slot 10, the politics screen's tooltips, by the element's name in this order: convoys_icon (POL_SW_CON_IRO / _DRO), convoys_val (0x5310D0), allies_icon (POL_SW_ALL_IRO / _DRO), allies_val (0x531110), bombs_icon (POL_SW_BOM_IRO / _DRO), bombs_val (0x531150), liberate_country (POL_LIB_COUNTRY_YES, or with no candidates POL_LIB_C_NO_FACTION / POL_LIB_C_WE_EXILE / POL_LIB_C_NO_EXILES / POL_LIB_C_POSSIBLE + a list), create_puppet (POL_PUPPET_YES / _NO), mobilize (POL_MOBILIZE_IRO + _DRO_V2 with DAYS + _DRO_V3 with MP; at war POL_MOBILIZE_WAR_IRO), demobilize (POL_DEMOBILIZE_IRO + _DRO; at war POL_DEMOBILIZE_WAR_IRO), revolt (GetMobilizeUndergroundsAvailability), faction_symbol_icon (the faction's name, delayed its rules and modifier), political_popularity_chart (the slice's ideology, its whole percent, delayed the change factors, a rule, the drift factors and QUALIFIES_FOR_CABINET), ruling_ideology_icon (the ruling party's name for the player), each `<ideology>_org` bar of org_chart (name: organisation, delayed the change factors), then the rows of minister_list1, minister_list2, laws_listbox, policies_listbox, law_list and policy_list through each row's own builder. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md, D.6.
addresses.evidence: 0x6BE790 to four `ret 8` exits (0x6BF767, 0x6C0D29, 0x6C0D5F, 0x6C0DC0) of one frame. The dispatch order and the keys are from the decompilation, checked on the listing for the pie (0x6BFFCD-0x6C0465: hit test 0xAA3270, slot 15 name, IntToString, 0x5287D0 on CCountry +0x10F4, the rule, 0x4F8490, 0x511550 with COUNT/QUALIFIES_FOR_CABINET and CCountry +0x112C), the org bars (0x6C05F0-0x6C0C00: slot 15 with the player's tag, ': ', FFP(+0x10C4[i], 2)) and the row branches (0x6C0CF6-0x6C0DCC: the call shapes of 0x6C2F60, 0x6B94C0, 0x6BA5A0, 0x6B9D80, 0x6BABC0). The mobilise, puppet, liberate and strategic-warfare text branches rest on the decompilation alone.

addresses.name: CCountryView::IsOpen

Held unchanged by CCountryView, CDiplomacyView, CEspionageView, CPoliticsView, CTechnologyView and CTheatreView; CInGameIdler::OpenCountryView asks it of every view.

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::BuildWidgets
addresses.comment: Hooks the buttons and makes the cabinet rows. create_puppet -> +0x1EC, liberate_country -> +0x220, mobilize -> +0x13C, demobilize -> +0x168, revolt -> +0x194, `back_button` of puppet_select and of liberate_select -> +0x1C0, `cancel` of minister_select_win -> +0xB8. Then empties minister_list1 and minister_list2 and, with n = (government positions - 1) / 2 (the position database counts its null at index 0), puts CMinisterItem('minister_entry', idler, view, position, 0, true) rows for positions 1..n in minister_list1 and n+1..last in minister_list2, in the database's order. Called by the constructor and by Rebuild.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6BCD10-0x6BD55B: each name pushed, the button's +0x48 observable given `lea [edi+N]`; the two list boxes' slot 23; the loop bounds from g_government_positions +0xC/+0x10 and the two `push 'minister_entry'; call 0x6C1D90` sites at 0x6BD345 and 0x6BD51E. EDI is the view at both call sites (0x6BB0E5 `mov edi, esi`, 0x6BB265). Bare `ret`.

addresses.comment: Calls slot 8 (CMinisterItem::Refresh) of every row of minister_list1 and then of minister_list2. From Show and from Update.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6BD560-0x6BD680: the two list boxes found through [edi+0xA8] slot 31, their slot 11 list walked (node +0 item, +8 next), item slot 8 (`[edx+0x20]`). Bare `ret`.

Only from the constructor and Rebuild - Show does not refill it.

addresses.comment: Empties laws_listbox and adds one CLawEntry for every law group from index 1 to the end of the law database's group vector (+0x28/+0x2C), each given the played country's law at that position of CCountry +0x628; then the list's slot 20. From Show, and from Update whenever a row's law is no longer the country's.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6BDB50-0x6BDD0C: country from the idler's slot 23 kept at [esp+0x10]; `mov esi,1`; the bound `[eax+0x2C]-[eax+0x28] sar 2`; `mov ecx,[edx+0x628]; mov ecx,[ecx+esi*4]` pushed to 0x6B91F0; the list's slot 4 with (row, 0). `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::FillOccupationList
addresses.comment: Empties policies_listbox and adds a CPolicyEntry for every country of the game state that owns a province, is not the played country, is at war with it (or either is REB), and has at least one owned province the played country controls - in the game state's country order. Then the list's slot 20.
addresses.evidence: From the decompilation only (0x6BDD10-0x6BDFC0, `ret 4`). Likely; the occupation policies are outside this reading's brief and their rows were not read on the listing.

addresses.name: CPoliticsView::FillPopularityChart
addresses.comment: The pie. total = sum of the played country's popularity (CCountry +0x10FC, from index 1). Where total > 1000 (1.000), for every ideology from index 1 in database order a slice of the ideology's colour (+0x54) and size round(p x 100000 / 1000 x 1000 / total / 1000.0) - the whole percent p x 100 / total, through single precision and `fistp` (round half to even); 0 below. Where total <= 1000 the pie is given no slices. Handed to the pie drawable (+0x254) through 0xAA37D0.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6BDFD0-0x6BE20E: the sum loop 0x6BE03E-0x6BE04E, `cmp edi,0x3E8; jle`, floorf(100000.5f) at 0x6BE0C9, __allmul/__alldiv by 1000, the divide by the total, `jns` floor at 0, divsd by 1000.0 (0x160A300), `fld/fistp`, 0x4385B0/0x438460 per slice, 0xAA37D0 at the end. `ret 4`.
